This suggests a potential mispricing in the stock, which could lead to undervaluation if market sentiment shifts towards more rational valuation. This further reinforces the notion that the stock may be undervalued, especially considering the sector benchmark P/B ratio is only 2.93x. The compounded profit growth over the last five years at 62% [E16] stands out as a strong positive indicator, indicating consistent and robust earnings performance despite recent negative trailing twelve months (TTM) profit growth of -62% [E18]. Furthermore, [E48] points out that price growth has exceeded profit growth by 25% recently, indicating expectations are running ahead of delivery. This suggests investors might be overly optimistic about future performance, which could lead to a correction in the stock price if these expectations do not materialize as anticipated.
